title: Cyberpunk 2077 Review
description: Cyberpunk 2077 review covering Night City, builds, combat, quests, Phantom Liberty and how the RPG holds up after years of major updates on modern platforms.
body:
A fair review of Cyberpunk 2077 in 2026 has to judge the game that exists now rather than simply replay the story of its 2020 launch. CD PROJEKT RED rebuilt major systems through Update 2.0, expanded the game with Phantom Liberty, brought the Ultimate Edition to Nintendo Switch 2 and Mac, and continued platform-specific work into 2026.

That makes the current review question more useful than whether the launch controversy has been redeemed. The real question is what kind of RPG Cyberpunk 2077 has become, where its strongest ideas now sit, and which limitations still matter after years of substantial revision.
author: Rouane Mounssif
imageAlt: Official Cyberpunk 2077 promotional artwork used as the review feature image.

cons: World reactivity can fall short of the presentation
Some role-playing consequences are narrower than expected
Technical experience still varies by platform
pros: Night City remains a striking setting
Major characters and quest lines are memorable
Build variety is much stronger after the 2.0 overhaul
Phantom Liberty strengthens the complete package
reviewMeta.verdict: Years of revision have turned Cyberpunk 2077 into a strong character-driven RPG whose greatest strengths remain Night City, quests and build freedom.

contentBlocks.text:
Update 2.0 overhauled several core systems, including perk progression, cyberware, the police system, enemy scaling, loot, crafting and parts of the game economy. Those changes affect the base game, so a current assessment has to treat them as the foundation rather than optional expansion features.

Later updates added more quality-of-life and platform support, making the modern version meaningfully different from the game that launched in 2020.
contentBlocks.heading: Cyberpunk 2077 in 2026 Is a Materially Different Game

contentBlocks.text:
Night City is more than a backdrop: districts, side jobs, environmental storytelling and the density of authored encounters give the city its identity. The strongest exploration comes when a location, character or mission changes how a neighborhood is understood.

The city is also a useful reminder that visual density and systemic reactivity are different strengths. Cyberpunk 2077 is often most convincing when its authored stories make the setting feel specific rather than when the open world is expected to simulate every possibility.
contentBlocks.heading: Night City Is the Center of the Experience

contentBlocks.text:
Update 2.0 replaced the original perk structure with a more focused system and made cyberware a central part of character development. Distinct attribute paths now support clearer approaches to stealth, hacking, mobility and direct combat.

The result is a progression model that emphasizes recognizable playstyle identities instead of simply accumulating incremental bonuses. Our [Cyberpunk 2077 beginner’s guide](/stories/cyberpunk-2077-beginners-guide/) provides a broader introduction to those systems for new players.
contentBlocks.heading: Progression Was Rebuilt Around Clearer Character Identities

contentBlocks.text:
Cyberpunk 2077 builds much of its role-playing identity around V, relationships, major story choices, side jobs and smaller encounters across Night City. Dialogue and mission outcomes can meaningfully reshape individual storylines, even when the wider city is less reactive than those authored quests suggest.

The distinction matters: the game’s strongest role-playing often lives inside specific character arcs and mission chains rather than broad simulation.
contentBlocks.heading: Quest Design Carries the Role-Playing Side

contentBlocks.text:
The modern game supports several broad approaches to encounters, including direct combat, stealth, hacking-focused builds and combinations of those styles. The rebuilt progression systems make those approaches more mechanically distinct than they were at launch.

Encounter variety depends heavily on how well a build’s abilities, cyberware and movement options reinforce one another across a long campaign.
contentBlocks.heading: Combat and Stealth Depend on Build Synergy

contentBlocks.text:
Phantom Liberty adds a major story set in Dogtown and is included with the base game in Cyberpunk 2077: Ultimate Edition. Because it was designed alongside the modernized systems, it is also a useful comparison point for mission structure, pacing and environmental density.

Phantom Liberty is discussed as part of the modern Cyberpunk 2077 package and current-version context.
contentBlocks.heading: Phantom Liberty Changes the Context of the Complete Package

contentBlocks.text:
Cyberpunk 2077’s modern supported versions span PC, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, Nintendo Switch 2 and Apple-silicon Mac, while the older PlayStation 4 and Xbox One editions do not represent the same current feature set.

Performance, image quality, controls, loading and remaining bugs can vary by platform; technical observations here refer to the PC version available through Steam.
contentBlocks.heading: The Technical Review Needs a Named Platform

contentBlocks.text:
Cyberpunk 2077’s revision history matters because it explains why current systems differ so much from the original release, but improvement itself is not a substitute for quality. The relevant question is how coherent and compelling the game is now.

That makes the modern experience the focus, while the launch history remains context rather than the verdict.
contentBlocks.heading: The Present Game Matters More Than Its Launch Reputation

quickRead: The modern 2.x-era game is materially different from the version released in 2020.
Night City remains the central strength, but atmosphere and world reactivity are not the same thing.
The rebuilt perk and cyberware systems give character progression clearer identities.
Phantom Liberty improves the complete package, but the review scope should state whether it is included in the score.
conclusion: Cyberpunk 2077 is best judged in the present tense. The modern RPG is defined by Night City, character-driven quest lines, clearer build identities and a long revision history that materially changed the underlying systems. Phantom Liberty further strengthens the complete package, but its inclusion in the final score needs to be explicit.\n\nFor readers entering Night City now, the [Cyberpunk 2077 beginner’s guide](/stories/cyberpunk-2077-beginners-guide/) and the dedicated [Cyberpunk 2077 game page](/games/cyberpunk-2077/) provide the clearest next steps while the verdict above reflects the current PC version reviewed through Steam.
